title: Step 2: A Library
story: Now a library holds many books. Adding changes the library, so these methods use a pointer receiver.
goal: Write Add (append a book) and Find (return the book with that title, or the error not found: TITLE).

tests.label: Find a book that was added
tests.expr: func() string { l := &Library{}; l.Add(Book{"Go", "Gopher", 2009}); b, err := l.Find("Go"); return fmt.Sprint(b, err) }()

tests.label: A missing book gives an error
tests.expr: func() string { l := &Library{}; l.Add(Book{"Go", "Gopher", 2009}); _, err := l.Find("Rust"); return fmt.Sprint(err) }()

tests.label: Add keeps every book
tests.expr: func() int { l := &Library{}; l.Add(Book{"A", "x", 1}); l.Add(Book{"B", "y", 2}); return len(l.books) }()

hints: Add: l.books = append(l.books, b). The receiver is a pointer so the change sticks.
Find: loop over l.books, return b, nil when the title matches, and errors.New("not found: " + title) at the end.
socratic: Why does Add need *Library and not Library?
What would happen to l.books if the receiver were a copy?
What should Find return in the Book position when it fails?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Step 2: A Library”?
